record_identity.title: Zillow exited Zillow Offers after home-price forecasting produced excessive business volatility

incident_identity.date_basis: Date follows the reviewed registry or primary occurrence record; no narrower time is inferred.

summary: Zillow announced the wind-down of Zillow Offers after concluding that unpredictability in forecasting home prices was greater than anticipated and that continued scaling would create excessive earnings and balance-sheet volatility. AI Incident Database records the occurrence as involving Zillow's machine-learning-assisted Zestimate and the shutdown included a reduction of approximately 25% of Zillow's workforce.

vigil_assessment.factual_basis: Zillow announced the wind-down of Zillow Offers after concluding that unpredictability in forecasting home prices was greater than anticipated and that continued scaling would create excessive earnings and balance-sheet volatility. AI Incident Database records the occurrence as involving Zillow's machine-learning-assisted Zestimate and the shutdown included a reduction of approximately 25% of Zillow's workforce.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: Zillow tied a capital-intensive home-buying operation to forecasts whose error and volatility proved harder to manage at scale than anticipated. The evidence supports a governance problem at the boundary between predictive uncertainty and business commitment, but it does not show that one model alone caused the shutdown.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: When forecasts drive purchases, inventory and balance-sheet exposure, uncertainty must constrain the scale and reversibility of the decisions built on them. Monitoring average model performance is insufficient if correlated forecast error can accumulate across a large portfolio before the organisation can exit safely.
assessment_boundaries: Zillow's announcement attributes the wind-down to greater-than-expected home-price forecasting unpredictability and resulting financial volatility, not to one isolated technical defect.
The record does not attribute all business losses or the workforce reduction solely to the Zestimate model.
Individual livelihood effects beyond the reported workforce reduction are not inferred.
The assessment does not reconstruct Zillow's private models, thresholds or acquisition decisions.
